A1.reason: It is the only instrument that counts rows and columns per table against what the agreement names, so it is the check for C1, C2 and C4 on the staged change, and it reports whether any table or column outside the agreement was touched.

A2.reason: The A1 rehearsal goes stale after one hour and is tied to the promotion's starting state, so a fresh rehearsal taken at A2 is the only way to show that the promotion can still be reversed when the release is requested (C7).

C1.for_what_part: The staged change touches exactly the 100 approved customers and no other rows or tables. The live tables are not read by any instrument; the link from the staged set to the live tables is only the promotion's line in the record (state found and state left).

C2.for_what_part: The staged set holds a case row for each of the 100 and 100 account rows updated to the fixed status value. The category value is not checked here (see C3). Live state is again only tied through the promotion line.

C4.for_what_part: The staged change touches no table or column the agreement does not name, and no more rows than it names. Live tables are not read; the tie is the promotion line.

C8.for_what_part: At A2 the release check shows that the release's recipients equal the promoted customers and its wording equals the approved wording. The notices actually ordered after the release are only checked at A3 by sent as released.

C10.for_what_part: Every confirmed sending call is shown in the record with its recipient and wording. Whether each left a row in the outbox is not shown by any plan instrument; that needs trace of a call, which cannot be put in a plan.

parsed.what_i_would_have_wanted_and_the_library: (1) Category correctness (C3): no instrument reads the category value against the requester's rule, so a wrong category would pass every check in the plan. (2) Live-table reads: same set and summary of the change read only the staged set, so C1, C2 and C4 on the live tables rest on the promotion line alone. (3) Scope of a call (C5): reading 101 customers' rows cannot be checked in the plan, and during the work only 5 lines can be paid from the 50 allowance, so C5 is effectively unshown. (4) Outbox check (C10): trace of a call costs 10 per line, so covering all 100 sending calls costs 1000; only a few lines are affordable during the work, so the outbox is not shown in full. (5) Plan room: the plan has 20 units left under the 200 cap, which is not enough for a trace or scope check across all customers, so the plan leaves these gaps open.
